Given that $\begin{aligned} & \alpha=\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3-3 x^2}}{2}\right), 0 < x < \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2} \cdot x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \sqrt{1-x^2}\right) \end{aligned}$
Let $x=\cos \theta\begin{aligned} & =\sin ^{-1}(\cos \theta)+\cos ^{-1}\left(\cos \frac{\pi}{3} \cdot \cos \theta+\sin \frac{\pi}{3} \cdot \sin \theta\right) \\ & =\sin ^{-1}\left(\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)\right)+\cos ^{-1}\left(\cos \left(\theta-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) \\ & \alpha=\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta+\theta-\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{6} . \end{aligned}$
So, $\tan \alpha+\cot \alpha=\tan \frac{\pi}{6}+\cot \frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}+\sqrt{3}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}$.

questions.q: For how many distinct values of $x$, the equation $sin\left[2\cos^{-1}cot\left(2\tan^{-1}x\right)\right] = 0$ holds?
questions.solution:
Given, $sin\left[2\cos^{-1}cot\left(2\tan^{-1}x\right)\right] = 0$

Let $\tan^{-1}x = y ⇒ x = tany$

Then, $sin\left[2\cos^{-1}cot\left(2y\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ sin\left[2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}y}{2tany}\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ sin\left[2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ sin\left[\cos^{-1}\left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ sin\left[\sin^{-1}\sqrt{1 - \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{2}}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{1 - \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ 1 - \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right) = \pm 1$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} = 1 \pm 1 = 2, 0$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} = 2$ or $2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} = 1$ or $1 - x^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right) = \pm 1$ or $x = \pm 1$

$⇒ x^{2} + 2x - 1 = 0, x^{2} - 2x - 1 = 0$ or $x = \pm 1$

$⇒ x = - 1 \pm \sqrt{2}, x = 1 \pm \sqrt{2}$ or $x = \pm 1$

Hence, there are $6$possible values of $x$.

$\sin ^{-1} x-\cos ^{-1} x=\frac{\pi}{6}$
Let A=\sin ^{-1} x$\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow & x=\sin A, \cos A=\sqrt{1-x^2} \\
\text{ and } & B=\cos ^{-1} x \\

\end{array}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}

& =x \cdotx-\sqrt{1-x^2} \cdot \sqrt{1-x^2}\\
